page: Amazon Web Services m8id.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides direct physical access to the underlying hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead. The server is powered by dedicated Intel processors operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 192 physical cores and 384 virtual CPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 1536.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. No graphics processing units are present in this configuration.

For high-throughput I/O requirements, the platform incorporates 22800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage. This substantial bundled solid-state capacity delivers low-latency direct read and write access, though local instance store data does not persist beyond instance termination. Networking capabilities feature a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large volume data transfers across distributed systems. The massive scale of 384 vCPUs combined with extensive high-speed NVMe storage provides high compute and I/O density in a single footprint, which improves operational efficiency for consolidated massive workloads compared to managing multiple smaller instances.

Because of its combined high core count, balanced memory footprint, high network throughput, and extensive local NVMe capacity, m8id.metal-96xl is structured for demanding production environments. Appropriate deployment targets include large-scale distributed databases, high-capacity in-memory data processing with local cache requirements, intensive extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, enterprise-grade continuous integration systems, and containerized microservice consolidation.
